request.prompt: A warm, sincere orchestral victory fanfare that settles into a gentle, loopable processional, at 108 BPM in 4/4 in a bright major key, relief more than triumph. For the first seven seconds: a short snare roll lifts into a section of French horns and trumpets playing a noble, open fanfare figure over timpani and a sweeping harp, and the orchestra lands on one clear, held major chord that rings out. Then, without a pause and without changing key or tempo, the music settles into a calm, steady, walking processional that lasts for the rest of the piece: pizzicato basses and soft snare brushes keep an easy stride, a solo trumpet and a solo horn trade a simple, dignified, hopeful tune, warm strings and a harp answer, and a soft timpani marks the downbeats. It never builds to a climax and never ends: it keeps the same easy stride so that it can repeat. Sincere and grateful, a little weary, never boastful. Real acoustic orchestra and real percussion recorded in a warm hall. No vocals. Steady tempo, no tempo changes, no fade-out, no final cadence. Not chiptune, not SNES, not arcade, no synthesizers, no electronic drums, no electric guitar, no pop.
